results.summary_before: This design implements a two-player Tic-Tac-Toe game using nine multiplexed common-cathode RGB LEDs and nine push-buttons. Pressing a button places a move in the corresponding cell, the logic evaluates the game state, and a separate RGB LED indicates the winner's colour when a winning combination is detected. Testing is done by wiring the Wokwi circuit with buttons, RGB LEDs and resistors and running the simulation at around 100 Hz or faster. The project is a complete interactive game on a single tile, with the main external requirement being the LED and button array.

results.summary_before: This Wokwi design sequentially displays the characters of the text "PILIPINASLASALLE" on a 7-segment display, one character per clock cycle, with the decimal point toggling each cycle. It includes a manual mode where the four BCD input pins select one of 16 predefined characters. The project is intended to be tested with a low-frequency clock (e.g., 1 Hz) and an external 7-segment display. Silicon tests show it working correctly on a demoboard.

results.summary_before: This design implements a side-scrolling 7-segment display with a programmable 16-character message memory. It is used by setting register-select switches to choose a memory location, setting character-encoding switches to the desired character, and toggling a write switch to load the character. An external board with an additional 7-segment display is required for full functionality. The documentation provides a character encoding table but no silicon test results.

results.summary_before: This Verilog design characterizes three flavors of 31-stage ring oscillators built from IHP SG13G2 standard cells, using a 24-bit asynchronous counter and a 10 ms sampling window. A 2-bit select chooses the oscillator flavor, and another 2-bit select reads out the low, mid, and high bytes of the captured count on the output pins. The design is enabled by a master enable pin and requires no external hardware beyond the standard Tiny Tapeout demo board. It is notable for being a silicon process and gate-delay characterization experiment using specific standard-cell flavors.

results.summary_before: This Verilog design implements an all-digital phase-locked loop with a bang-bang phase detector, an up/down counter loop filter, and a ring-oscillator DCO. The PLL locks onto the input reference clock after reset, and the generated clock, lock indicator, and reference clock are available on output pins, while the 7-bit frequency control word is exposed on bidirectional pins for debugging. An oscilloscope is needed to measure the output frequency. The design is notable for being a fully digital PLL implementation on a Tiny Tapeout tile.

results.summary_before: This Verilog design implements a third-order CIC filter with a decimation ratio of 32 to demodulate a 1-bit PDM signal into 8-bit PCM audio data. It is intended to work with an external discrete second-order delta-sigma modulator on a custom PCB, with the PDM input on ui[0] and the PCM output on uo[7:0]. Testing involves generating a 10 kHz sine wave with a Digilent Analog Discovery, feeding it through the PCB, and observing the reconstructed waveform on a logic analyzer while synchronizing clocks at 2.048 MHz. The project focuses on hardware-in-the-loop verification between a custom analog board and the ASIC.
